stories.title: The next ayahuasca? Gabon fights to protect sacred plant from US drug companies
summary: Iboga root, central to several Gabonese ritual traditions, is believed to have huge potential for use in treating addiction and some mental illnessesThe temple is dark, its sandy floor edged with candles.
People sit shoulder to shoulder beneath palm fronds hung from the rafters.

Through the night, they swallow what they have come here for: a bitter root bark called iboga.Tabernanthe iboga is a slow-growing central African rainforest shrub, the root bark of which has long been used in several Gabonese ritual traditions.

stories.title: US workers facing deadly heat borrow from tomato pickers to win key protections
summary: As efforts to protect people from extreme heat stall, organizers are embracing an approach that targets major brands’ reputations“It’s the kind of heat that makes you feel like you’re being dehydrated, like your skin is drying out,” said Lucas Benitez, after harvesting watermelons with his sons and wife this summer. “The heat that we had 30 years ago is not nearly the heat that we have today.”This summer was the hottest on record in the US, and most workers in fields, greenhouses and unconditioned indoor facilities still do not have heat protections on the job, putting their health at risk as the climate crisis is expected to make extreme heat more frequent and intense.

stories.title: Small business owners are doing OK – but will that help Trump overcome his low approval ratings?
summary: Overall, economic sentiment for Trump is poor, but small businesses seem fairly confident, according to several surveysThere are 34m small businesses in the United States.
They employ approximately half of the country’s workers and generate about half of the country’s GDP.
Overall, economic sentiment for Donald Trump is poor but small business – admittedly a diverse demographic that’s hard to poll – seems fairly confident.

stories.title: World leaders must wise up to threat of cyber-attacks or rogue fridges will be least of their worries | Heather Stewart
summary: Global cooperation seems unlikely despite AI increasing the risk of digital fraud and the need to protect the financial systemRogue French fridges were an unlikely talking point for the world’s leading economists, central bankers and finance chiefs meeting in a sultry Bangkok last week – helping to underline the spiralling cost of cyber-attacks.Kristalina Georgieva, the managing director of the International Monetary Fund, seized on news that supermarket chains across France had to chuck out piles of spoiled food after hackers accessed their fridge controls and turned up the temperature to 50C.

stories.title: Condé Nast’s UK profits drop by more than a third as sale of Vogue publisher ruled out
summary: Magazine group points to restructuring bill but says it ‘remains profitable in the UK for another year’Profits at Condé Nast’s UK arm slumped by more than a third last year, according to figures published shortly after the billionaire family that owns the luxury magazine group and titles from Vogue to GQ ruled out a sale.The publisher, which enjoyed a bumper 2024 after booking £64m in proceeds from the sale of its UK headquarters Vogue House in London, saw pre-tax profits excluding exceptional items tumble 36% from £28m that year to nearly £18m last year.

stories.title: The last lace mill – in pictures
summary: MYB Textiles Ltd is the last mill in the world weaving patterned Nottingham lace on traditional looms.
Once there were 20 lace mills in the Irvine Valley towns of Newmilns and Darvel alone.
The lace industry became the largest employer in the area for a time and flourished until the late 1970s when competition emerged from other European countries and Asia.

stories.title: £3,500 and no work done: the offer to help that’s really a roofing scam
summary: Citizens Advice warns of its No 1 scam as growing number of people are targeted by criminals posing as roofersThe builder who calls at your door says they are doing some work in the area and has spotted a loose tile on your roof.
They offer to fix it for a good price that you agree to.But when they go up on their ladder to inspect the problem, they see another problem.
The only solution, the builder says, is to have rigid PVC trays installed to divert the water.

stories.title: Hiding in plane sight: the invisible turbulence that can strike out of a clear blue sky
summary: As the planet warms, airlines are grappling with what this means for air travel – and for the passengers who simply refuse to keep their seatbelts fastenedIt was a swelteringly hot afternoon in south-west Myanmar on 21 May 2024.

But for Singapore Airlines flight SQ321 passing just above, it was anything but benign.In the cabin of the Boeing 777, passengers were being woken up for breakfast with three hours to go on the journey from London to Singapore.
At 2.19pm and 23 seconds local time, moderate turbulence shook the plane for 17 seconds and the seatbelt sign was switched on.

stories.title: Elon Musk agrees to settle lawsuits over 2024 election lottery
summary: Trump-boosting billionaire was sued over promise to give away $1m per day to random signatories of petitionElon Musk and his ⁠America Pac political action committee said recently that they agreed to settle two ⁠proposed class ⁠actions ​alleging the billionaire entrepreneur defrauded residents in closely contested states before the ⁠2024 US election by promising voters a lottery-style daily $1m giveaway.The plaintiffs, Musk and America Pac ​told the ‌judge overseeing the two ‌related lawsuits in federal court in Austin, Texas, ‌on Thursday that they have reached settlements subject to court approval.

stories.title: Move over, pervert glasses – the latest toxic trend is robogroping
summary: Whenever a new technology is created, it will, without exception, immediately be used to harass girls and womenYou may be familiar with rule 34 of the internet, which states that if something exists or can be imagined, there will almost certainly be online porn of it.
Now let me introduce my rule 35: whenever a new technology is created, it will, without exception, immediately be used to harass girls and women.See, for example, Meta’s “pervert glasses”.
Indeed, at the Meta Connect 2026 keynote, Mark Zuckerberg did not feel the need to apologize to the women whose lives have been upended by his technology.

stories.title: Inside the long, bitter fight over one man’s quest to build the biggest AI datacenter in California
summary: A modern-day prospector promised rural Imperial thousands of jobs and millions in tax revenue – but his plan has set off a firestorm of resistanceSebastian Rucci zoomed in on a map in late 2024, looking closely at a large block of brown earth.
It was in the Sonoran desert, just north of the Mexican border, where temperatures regularly rose past 100F (37.8C).
And then, there was the city of Imperial – population 22,000 – to win over.

stories.title: Bank of England governor walks out of IMF summit in protest against Russia
summary: Andrew Bailey among finance leaders to leave session in Bangkok when Russian finance minister addressed groupThe Bank of England governor, Andrew Bailey, has taken part in a walkout of finance leaders who left an International Monetary Fund meeting in protest against Russian involvement.Bailey joined counterparts from France, Germany and a number of Scandinavian and Baltic countries who left the session in Bangkok when the Russian finance minister, Anton Siluanov, addressed the group in Russian.

stories.title: US corporate lobbyists mounted ‘blitz’ to dilute landmark EU deforestation law, report finds
summary: Environmental watchdog Mighty Earth reveals two-year effort to postpone and weaken EU Deforestation RegulationUS corporate lobbyists launched a two-year “blitz” to postpone and weaken the world’s most progressive legislation to protect forests, according to a new investigation by the environmental watchdog Mighty Earth.Major US firms and trade associations, including Cargill, Bunge, Mondelēz and the US Soybean Export Council, as well as numerous other US firms and organizations, sought to influence the EU Deforestation Regulation (EUDR) in more than 350 meetings, the advocacy group found.

I don’t want to follow in the footsteps of my friend, who knows that the ads at her local run for 22 minutes so slinks in at just the right time.

stories.title: Squash down: smaller pumpkins expected this Halloween after drought in England
summary: Data shows 2026 could be worst harvest on record, as growers suggest painting faces on vegetables instead of carvingIn the lead-up to Halloween, front porches across the country feature fat, proudly carved pumpkins, lit from within by tea lights.But this year there is likely to be a shortage due to drought, experts have warned, with the squashes much smaller than usual.

stories.title: Stinky business: south London bike shop hit by ‘unbearable’ stench from Thames Water sewer
summary: Owner and mechanics fear for their health and future of the Herne Hill shop with no date for fixing problemThe leafy south London neighbourhood of Herne Hill is a haven for cyclists who can often be seen lapping the local parks and refuelling at the many cafes that line the suburban streets.

But there is something foul in the air of this corner of the capital – and for once it’s not the traffic fumes hitting bicycle riders.A toxic stench thought to be caused by untreated sewage stuck in Thames Water drains has been emanating from the subterranean depths for months, most likely caused by the summer’s lack of rain.

stories.title: Plan to make firms pay more to train older workers than youth apprentices in England
summary: Exclusive: Ministers considering overhaul of apprenticeship funding scheme to tackle youth jobs crisisEmployers in England are to be forced to pay more to train an older worker than a youth apprentice under plans being drawn up by the government to tackle the youth jobs crisis.The Guardian understands ministers plan to overhaul Labour’s apprenticeship funding scheme to increase the cost of training by 25% for a worker over the age of 25 in order to encourage businesses to train young people instead.
